esp32_hardware.psram_bus_bandwidth: SPI quad mode ~40-80 MB/s (approx 4-5x slower than internal SRAM)
esp32_hardware.hardware_fpu: Single-precision FPU (scalar only, no SIMD / NEON vector acceleration)

blockers.title: Severe Memory Overflow
blockers.detail: INT8 YAMNet weights (3789.1 KB) plus activation arena (1850.0 KB) require 5703.1 KB RAM, which exceeds the total 4096 KB PSRAM by 1607.1 KB (139% of total capacity).

blockers.title: Severe Real-Time Latency Violation
blockers.detail: Estimated total inference pipeline takes ~4370 ms on ESP32 Xtensa LX6 @ 240 MHz. This is 4.4x slower than real time (budget: 1000 ms). Audio ring buffers would immediately overflow, dropping 75% of incoming audio.

blockers.title: Resampling & Dual-Model Complexity
blockers.detail: YAMNet strictly requires 16,000 Hz audio. The INMP441 capture is locked at 22,050 Hz to match the production filterbank. Performing on-chip decimation/interpolation adds 65 ms of CPU overhead per second.

recommendations: Do NOT deploy YAMNet directly on the ESP32-WROVER-B.
Deploy Model B (Expanded-Data CNN) converted to INT8 TFLite on the ESP32. It maintains sub-400 ms latency and fits comfortably in 532 KB.
If YAMNet's superior general feature representation is desired, use it as a desktop/server-side secondary validator when the ESP32 flags an ambiguous rattle event.
Alternatively, explore Knowledge Distillation where YAMNet acts as a teacher guiding Model B's training.
